Schedule SE-led throughput deep dive and latency tail benchmark
Share SOC2 attestation + KMS integration notes
Provision 2-week dedicated trial cluster for EU region

Liam O'Connor: Run projected 99th-pct latency numbers for ArborCloud traffic profile and share results (due 2026-11-13)
Sofia Mendes / ArborCloud: Share current KMS provider details and compliance contact (due 2026-11-11)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-09 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Felix (Redwood CSM), Jesse (ArborCloud Head of Platform), Rana (SRE Lead), Sofia (CISO), Tom (Procurement)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer evaluating consolidation of EU and APAC capacity under a single renewal to simplify billing and failover. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC, pricing constructs, SLA concerns, and compliance needs (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Agreed to a short dedicated trial in EU and follow-up technical deep-dive to validate latency and throughput targets. Redwood to send revised blended quote and security docs.
topics: Renewal term options and blended pricing
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jesse (ArborCloud): Jesse here, Rana, Sofia, Tom on my side.
[00:10] Maya (Redwood): Great. So agenda: renewal options, capacity consolidation across EU/APAC, and next steps — aiming to keep this short.
[00:18] Rana (ArborCloud): Yeah sounds good. We're at the point where our usage spiked Q3, and the separate region SKUs are making ops messy.
[00:24] Liam (Redwood SE): Mm-hmm. Just to call out from a capacity standpoint — when you consolidate, there are a couple levers: reserved capacity in Dedicated, geo-fault domains, and optional private footprint if you need VPC isolation.
[00:36] Sofia (CISO): On our side security is top. We need to confirm SOC2 status, cross-region key rotation, KMS integrations — we use KeyVault and AWS KMS depending on account.
[00:46] Maya (Redwood): Understood. We have SOC2 Type II; I'll share the attestation. KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM — there's a doc I'll drop.
[00:55] Tom (Procurement): Quick one on commercial — if we consolidate EU and APAC onto a single renewal, do we get a blended rate or is pricing per region?
[01:03] Maya (Redwood): You can structure it as blended or regionized. Blended often easier for ops, and we can show a model that keeps unit costs predictable. We'll produce a few scenarios: flat blended SKU, and an alternate that keeps separate SKUs but offers a volume discount.
[01:15] Jesse (ArborCloud): Our preference would be one invoice and simpler failover. Latency is the other concern though — some APAC traffic needs lower tail latency.
[01:22] Liam (Redwood SE): Right — we should baseline your 95th and 99th percentile latency. For Dedicated we see consistent 99th p90 tails; with Sticky KV cache and prefix caching we can hit your numbers but we should validate with your exact prompt lengths.
[01:35] Rana (ArborCloud): We've got a mix of short query chat (8–32 tokens mostly) and longer summarization runs for ingestion jobs. The ingest jobs are batched overnight so throughput matters there.
[01:44] Liam (Redwood SE): That helps. For short chat, dedicated with continuous batching and small sequence kernels will be cheapest and lowest latency; for long summarizations you benefit from quantized variants for cost savings.
[01:55] Sofia (CISO): Also need audit logs for all inference calls — we can't have PII leak. Do you retain request logs? What's retention and access?
[02:04] Maya (Redwood): We have per-customer audit logs, and retention is configurable per contract. For Private deployments customers control retention; Hosted has default retention with add-on options for longer retention. We'll provide the security page link.
[02:15] Tom (Procurement): Any other vendors we should be aware of? We had internal RFP responses from VertexAI and CloudModelX.
[02:22] Felix (Redwood CSM): Noted. Competitively, VertexAI quoted similar latencies but their private/onprem path was slower to stand up. Anthropic was also mentioned in the RFP.
[02:33] Jesse (ArborCloud): Okay, so what would a trial look like? We want to smoke-test EU region with our production traffic pattern for two weeks.
[02:40] Liam (Redwood SE): We can provision a small Dedicated pool in eu-west and mirror a subset of production traffic — ideally a 10% sampler to capture latency tail. We'll enable KV prefix caching and turn on quantization where appropriate.
[02:50] Rana (ArborCloud): How long does provisioning take? We have an internal release in late November and want trial results before then.
[02:56] Felix (Redwood CSM): Typical provisioning for Dedicated trial is 3–5 business days once the order is confirmed. We'll prioritize EU since it's the blocker.
[03:05] Maya (Redwood): I'll kick off the quote today and tag provisioning as 'expedite' — we'll aim to have the trial cluster ready by 11/16.
[03:12] Tom (Procurement): On the contract term, are we able to extend mid-term if usage grows? We want flexibility for burst capacity.
[03:19] Maya (Redwood): Yes — Dedicated contracts allow commit bands and reserved pools with burst lanes. You can increase committed capacity mid-term; pricing is typically pro-rated. We'll include burst pricing tables in the quote.
[03:28] Jesse (ArborCloud): SLA targets? We need 99.9% availability for critical APIs and a latency SLO for the 95th under load.
[03:36] Liam (Redwood SE): SLA is configurable — 99.9% can be included for Dedicated with an enterprise SLA. For latency SLOs we can set per-route targets and configure automatic fallback to a higher-capacity variant.
[03:46] Sofia (CISO): And compliance for data residency — if data must remain in EU for certain routes, can we pin model serving to eu-west?
[03:53] Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, routing policies allow region pinning per-route. For Private deployments you control the network. For Hosted we'll ensure EU clusters only handle those routes.
[04:01] Rana (ArborCloud): Any risk of cross-region KV cache leaking between tenants?
[04:06] Liam (Redwood SE): No cross-tenant sharing — KV caches are per-tenant and per-model instance. There have been occasional transcriptions where 'KV cash' appears in logs, sorry — bad joke — but it's isolated.
[04:17] Jesse (ArborCloud): Haha. Okay. On the technical deep-dive, we need numbers: token/sec, 99th tail latency, and cost per 1M tokens for our mix.
[04:25] Liam (Redwood SE): We'll run your ingestion and chat profiles through our bench harness. I'll provide a spreadsheet with token/mix projections and projected cost under blended vs regionized SKUs.
[04:34] Tom (Procurement): Can you also put together a short annex on termination/exit — e.g., data export, transfer of keys, and handover steps?
[04:41] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely, we'll include a migration/exit annex and timeline.
[04:44] Sofia (CISO): For KMS we use both Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS depending on the environment. Do you support both?
[04:50] Liam (Redwood SE): Yes, we integrate with both. For Private we can also support HSM-backed BYOK processes. We'll need your key policy contact to coordinate.
[04:58] Jesse (ArborCloud): Great. Anything else on contracts?
[05:02] Maya (Redwood): Two commercial options: 12-month with blended discount, or 24-month with higher committed discount plus guaranteed capacity. Which is preferred?
[05:11] Tom (Procurement): Likely 12-month to start, with optional 12-month renewal clause — want flexibility.
[05:15] Felix (Redwood CSM): That's common. We'll model a 12-month with an uplift clause that lets you add capacity mid-term at negotiated tiers.
[05:23] Rana (ArborCloud): One more on observability — token-level breakdown by route, per-request tracing. We need that integrated with our Datadog.
[05:31] Liam (Redwood SE): We have tracing hooks and can emit to Datadog via our tracing exporter. Will include integration steps in the tech readout.
[05:38] Jesse (ArborCloud): Ok let's recap.
[05:41] Maya (Redwood): Recap: Redwood to send blended and regionized quote, include burst lanes and exit annex; Redwood SE to run latency/cost bench and produce spreadsheet; Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS integration docs; Provision EU Dedicated trial (2 weeks) targeted for 11/16 — ArborCloud to share KMS contacts and sample traffic profiles.
[05:55] Sofia (CISO): We'll get KMS contact and compliance owner over by 11/11.
[05:59] Tom (Procurement): Procurement will review quotes on 11/13.
[06:03] Maya (Redwood): Great. Anything else?
[06:06] Jesse (ArborCloud): No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[06:08] Maya (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up with notes and the quote. Bye.
[06:12] [meeting ends]

Note: Transcript includes natural disfluencies and occasional mis-transcriptions typical of human speech; timestamps approximate.
